items.en: Trump defends Putin relationship, warns AI data centres must stay in US
items.zh: 川普為對普丁關係辯護，並警告 AI 資料中心必須留在美國
items.summary: At a wide-ranging news conference, US President Donald Trump defended his working relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying dialogue remains necessary. He also discussed the war in Iran and praised his recent trip to China. Most notably for markets, Trump warned that American technology companies must build their artificial intelligence data centres inside the United States, threatening what he called a tremendous tax on firms that site that capacity abroad. The remarks landed during a week of heavy selling in AI-linked shares and add policy uncertainty to an already fragile semiconductor and data-centre investment outlook.

items.en: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Putin ally declares 'no one needs Europe'
items.zh: 烏克蘭襲擊刻赤大橋，普丁盟友稱「沒人需要歐洲」
items.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, using weapons and communications technology it developed domestically rather than systems supplied by Western partners. The attack on the symbolically important span came as rhetoric between Moscow and European capitals sharpened further, with a senior Putin ally dismissing Europe's relevance outright. Analysts read the strike as evidence that Kyiv's home-grown deep-strike capability is maturing even as foreign military aid becomes less predictable, and as a signal that Russia-Europe tensions are widening beyond the battlefield into trade, borders and energy.

items.en: Israeli drone attacks kill seven Palestinians in central Gaza
items.zh: 以色列無人機攻擊造成加薩中部七名巴勒斯坦人死亡
items.summary: Seven Palestinians were killed in Israeli drone attacks in central Gaza, with residents describing widespread fear and panic as unmanned aircraft operated overhead. The strikes continued despite the ceasefire framework that is formally still in place, underlining how little protection the agreement has offered civilians in practice. Aid groups say repeated attacks are obstructing the delivery of food, fuel and medical supplies into the Strip, and that displaced families have no reliably safe area to move to. The deaths add to a toll that has kept rising through the supposed truce period.

items.en: Russia complains of 'new Iron Curtain' as Estonia shuts its borders
items.zh: 愛沙尼亞關閉陸路邊界，俄羅斯抱怨出現「新鐵幕」
items.summary: Estonia closed its road border crossings with Russia following an attack on a drone manufacturer on Estonian soil, prompting Moscow to accuse the European Union of erecting a new Iron Curtain. Tallinn framed the closure as a security measure against sabotage and hybrid operations rather than a diplomatic rupture. The move tightens an already hardening frontier along NATO's eastern flank, where Baltic states have steadily restricted travel, trade and airspace access. It also raises the practical question of how cross-border family, freight and transit traffic will be handled in the months ahead.

items.en: Protests held across Europe over wages, services, high living costs
items.zh: 歐洲多國爆發抗議，訴求工資、公共服務與高生活成本
items.summary: Workers and students took to the streets in cities across Europe to protest stagnant wages, cuts to public services and a cost of living that has outpaced incomes. The demonstrations, inspired by sustained protest movements in France, show no sign of abating and have drawn in teachers, transport staff and university students alike. Organisers are pressing governments to reverse austerity measures and raise minimum pay, while several administrations face the prospect of rolling strike action through the winter. Economists warn the unrest could complicate fiscal plans already strained by defence and energy commitments.

items.en: Trump calls for Nvidia to reinstate 'brilliant' Jensen Huang
items.zh: 川普呼籲 Nvidia 讓「出色的」黃仁勳回任執行長
items.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly urged Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang, calling the former chief executive brilliant and saying the company should give him a second chance, while also suggesting Huang owes the public a big apology. Huang's abrupt departure has become a central narrative in the current AI-stock rout: Nvidia shares fell 13.8 per cent on Friday as investors weighed leadership uncertainty alongside doubts about the durability of data-centre spending. The intervention is unusual in mixing presidential pressure with the governance of a private company at a volatile moment.

items.en: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across US after California ban
items.zh: 加州下令禁止後，Waymo 全美暫停無人駕駛高速公路載客
items.summary: Waymo suspended driverless freeway rides across the United States after California regulators banned the practice, having declared self-driving cars an imminent hazard to public safety following a series of traffic incidents. The suspension is the broadest operational retreat yet for a company that had been expanding highway autonomy city by city. Regulators want data on how the vehicles handle merging, debris and emergency vehicles at speed before service resumes. For the wider robotaxi sector the decision resets expectations: surface-street operations continue, but the freeway milestone that underpinned growth forecasts is now on hold.

items.en: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews after 13-year wait
items.zh: 《俠盜獵車手 6》歷經 13 年等待上市，獲得滿堂彩
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launched to overwhelmingly positive reviews after a thirteen-year gap since its predecessor, with critics calling it a masterpiece, spectacular, and an astonishing American epic. The release is the largest entertainment launch of the year by revenue expectations and a rare bright spot in a technology sector otherwise dominated by AI-valuation anxiety. Beyond the reviews, the launch is being watched as a test of whether a single premium title can still move an entire industry's numbers, and of how well servers and storefronts cope with simultaneous global demand.

items.en: Nations League quarterfinal draw: Spain face France, England play Norway
items.zh: 國家聯賽八強抽籤：西班牙對法國、英格蘭對挪威
items.summary: The UEFA Nations League quarterfinal draw paired Spain with France and England with Norway, setting up two of the most anticipated ties the competition has produced. Spain against France revisits a rivalry that has decided recent major-tournament semifinals, while England's meeting with Norway offers a test against one of Europe's most improved attacking sides. The knockout round carries added weight this cycle because results feed into seeding for subsequent qualifying campaigns. Both fixtures will be played over two legs, with venues and exact kick-off times to be confirmed by the governing body.

items.en: 'Total error of judgement': Drone operator removes United training footage
items.zh: 「完全判斷失誤」：無人機操作者撤下曼聯訓練影片
items.summary: A drone operator removed footage of a Manchester United training session from the internet and issued an apology, describing the decision to film and upload it as a total error of judgement. The video captured new manager Mauricio Pochettino's first session with the squad, material clubs guard closely because it reveals tactical shape and personnel plans. The episode has renewed calls within English football for clearer rules on airspace above training grounds, and for sanctions where private sessions are recorded without consent. United have not said whether they will pursue further action.

items.en: Kenya's growing doping crisis overshadows legacy as athletics powerhouse
items.zh: 肯亞興奮劑危機持續擴大，掩蓋其田徑強權的輝煌傳統
items.summary: More than 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit since 2017, most of them distance runners, in a doping crisis that now overshadows the country's standing as the sport's dominant endurance nation. Investigators point to unregulated supplements, informal medical advice in training camps and the financial pressure on athletes chasing prize money as drivers. Kenyan officials have promised more testing and education, but critics say enforcement remains thin outside elite squads. The scale of the sanctions has prompted debate about whether the country risks competition restrictions.

items.en: South Korea cheating scandal: Are AI smart glasses a threat to exams?
items.zh: 韓國作弊風波：AI 智慧眼鏡成為考試的新威脅？
items.summary: A cheating scandal in South Korea has focused attention on whether AI-enabled smart glasses can defeat conventional exam invigilation. The devices look like ordinary eyewear but can capture question papers and relay answers in real time, leaving proctors with little visual cue that anything is wrong. Education authorities are weighing device bans, signal jamming and redesigned question formats that reward reasoning over recall. The episode matters well beyond Korea: high-stakes university entrance systems everywhere rest on the assumption that a supervised room is a sealed room, and that assumption is now in question.

items.en: Young French students who see 'no change' keep up protests in Paris suburbs
items.zh: 看不到改變的法國年輕學生，持續在巴黎郊區抗爭
items.summary: Students in the Paris suburbs are continuing protests that began over education reform, saying they see no change in schools that remain underfunded and overcrowded. Many of those interviewed describe a sense that promises made after earlier rounds of unrest were quietly dropped once media attention moved on. Their grievances combine class sizes and teacher shortages with longer-standing complaints about opportunity and policing in the banlieues. The persistence of the movement among younger pupils, rather than university students alone, is what distinguishes this wave and makes it harder for the government to wait out.

items.en: Thousands demand cancellation of Nathan Cofnas talk at Oxford University
items.zh: 數千人要求牛津大學取消 Nathan Cofnas 的演講
items.summary: Thousands of people signed demands that Oxford University cancel a scheduled talk by academic Nathan Cofnas, reopening a long-running argument about where academic freedom ends and institutional endorsement begins. Supporters of the event argue that universities exist precisely to host contested claims and that cancellation sets a precedent for any unpopular research. Opponents counter that a platform is not neutral and that some arguments cause measurable harm to students who must then study alongside them. The dispute is a familiar one on campuses, but the scale of the petition has made it a national story.

items.en: US tech sell-off continues as Anthropic tumbles after mega IPO
items.zh: Anthropic 掛牌後重挫，美國科技股賣壓延續
items.summary: Anthropic's shares fell sharply in their second session, closing down 9.1 per cent at $88.30 against an IPO price of $83 and a first-day peak of $115.10. The listing had been treated as a potential confidence boost for an AI industry struggling to regain its footing, so the reversal intensified the broader sell-off instead. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 10.7 per cent on the same day, with Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom all falling more than twelve per cent. Investors are now openly questioning whether AI capital spending plans can be financed at current valuations.

items.en: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
items.zh: 美國六個月內核准近 90 萬顆 AI 晶片銷往中國
items.summary: A US House committee released export data showing Washington approved sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China over a six-month period, a figure far larger than most observers had assumed given the stated policy of restricting advanced compute. The disclosure came amid scrutiny of a former Nvidia chief executive's alleged links to a Chinese intelligence operation. Lawmakers from both parties called the volume incompatible with national-security goals and signalled they will push for tighter licensing. For chipmakers, the data cuts both ways: it reveals real China demand and the regulatory risk attached to it.

items.en: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown
items.zh: 美國國會議員推動更嚴格的 AI 晶片出口規範
items.summary: US lawmakers are pressing for tougher rules on AI chip exports as the administration tightens its China crackdown, proposing lower performance thresholds, per-customer volume caps and mandatory tracking of where accelerators physically end up. Industry groups warn that the measures would push Chinese buyers toward domestic alternatives and cost American vendors a market they cannot easily replace. The debate arrives as the sector's valuations are already under pressure, making policy risk a live variable for earnings forecasts rather than a distant one, and keeping semiconductor supply-chain names volatile into year-end.

items.en: Kenshi Yonezu brings GHOST World Tour to Taipei Dome on 26-27 December
items.zh: 米津玄師 12/26–27 登上台北大巨蛋，首次個人巨蛋公演
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu's 2026-2027 world tour GHOST reaches Taipei Dome for two nights on 26 and 27 December 2026, with doors at 15:00 and the show starting at 18:00 on both days. Listed ticket prices run from NT$1,800 to NT$5,980, with accessible seating at NT$2,240 and NT$2,840. It is billed as his first solo show at the Taipei Dome, a considerable step up from the Taipei Arena dates that Japanese headliners usually take. No ticket on-sale date is stated for the Taipei legs yet, so watch the promoter's channels.

items.en: YOASOBI release new single 'KILLA' during ongoing Chouwakusei tour
items.zh: YOASOBI 於「超惑星」巡演期間發行新曲〈KILLA〉
items.summary: YOASOBI have released a new digital single titled KILLA, revealing its cover artwork at the same time, and published live footage of the song taken from their current Chouwakusei arena tour. The duo have been playing the track on the road ahead of the release, a pattern they have used before to build familiarity before streaming day. The tour itself continues through the winter with dates across Japan, and the group has previously extended similar runs into Asian markets, so Taiwan and Hong Kong fans have reason to watch for an added leg.

items.en: LiSA maps out 19-date LACE UP live run across 2026 and 2027
items.zh: LiSA 公布 LACE UP 巡演，橫跨 2026 至 2027 共 19 場
items.summary: LiSA's LACE UP live run is laid out across 2026 and 2027 with nineteen performances, with dates, venues and ticket details compiled per show. The schedule follows her LiVE is Smile Always 15th-anniversary shows, which took in Taipei Arena in June 2026 alongside Hong Kong and Seoul stops, so an Asian extension to this run is plausible but is not yet announced. For fans in Taiwan the practical point is to track the Japanese dates now, since overseas legs for her tours have typically been confirmed only after the domestic schedule is largely sold.
